mekayis.metin:
(يَهَّ) الْيَاءُ وَالْهَاءُ. يَقُولُونَ: يَهْيَهَ بِالْإِبِلِ، إِذَا قَالَ: يَاهْ يَاهْ.
[بَابُ الْيَاءِ وَمَا بَعْدَهَا مِمَّا جَاءَ عَلَى ثَلَاثَةِ أَحْرُفٍ]
ٍ وَكَتَبْتُ ذَلِكَ كُلَّهُ بَابًا وَاحِدًا لِقِلَّتِهِ
mekayis.metin_tr: (يَهَّ) Yâ ile Hâ'dır. Derler ki: bir adam develerine 'yâh yâh' diye seslendiğinde, buna develeri 'yâh yâh' ile çağırmak (يَهْيَهَ بِالْإِبِلِ) denir. [Yâ bâbı ve üç harf üzerine kurulmuş olanlardan onun ardından gelenler] Bunların tümünü, sayıları pek az olduğu için tek bir bâb hâlinde yazdım.

يَؤُهْ • (yaʔuh) (form I) /ja.ʔuh/
# third-person masculine singular non-past active jussive of آهَ (ʔāha)

anlam: Used to form abstract nouns from other nouns and from adjectives. Usually there is a parallel nisba adjective in ـِيّ (-iyy), with a parallel meaning. For example, اِشْتِرَاكِيَّة (ištirākiyya, “socialism”) is formed from اِشْتِرَاك (ištirāk, “sharing, cooperation”), with a corresponding nisba adjective اِشْتِرَاكِيّ (ištirākiyy, “socialist”). It is possible to analyze cases like these as e.g. اِشْتِرَاكِيّ (ištirākiyy, “socialist”) suffixed with ـَة (-a) to form an abstract noun. However, there are other cases, such as جَاذِبِيَّة (jāḏibiyya, “attraction, gravity”) derived from جَاذِب (jāḏib, “attractive”) or أَهَمِّيَّة (ʔahammiyya, “importance”) derived from أَهَمّ (ʔahamm, “more important”), of formation of nisba nouns from non-nisba adjectives where no corresponding nisba adjective exists.
Used to form nouns of various types from other nouns, e.g. device nouns such as بُنْدُقِيَّة (bunduqiyya, “rifle”) from بُنْدُق (bunduq, “hazelnut, bullet”).
